articles.title: Chiefs WR Rashee Rice reportedly files for bankruptcy, citing $3.45 million in debts following fallout from 2024 car crash
articles.summary: Rice reportedly claimed that he owes $2.1 million as a result of multiple civil lawsuits.
articles.body:
Kansas City Chiefs wide receiver Rashee Rice has filed for bankruptcy, according to court filings obtained by multiple outlets. In the filings, Rice reportedly claims that he has more than $3.45 million in debts.

A significant chunk of Rice's debt, per the filing, stems from several lawsuits the receiver has faced over the past year. Rice was sued by multiple victims of a Dallas car crash he was part of in 2024 and was sued in February by an ex-girlfriend who alleged that he physically abused her for more than a year.

Rice, who reportedly filed the claim in the Northern District of Texas bankruptcy court, says that more that $2.1 million of his debts are tied to the lawsuits. The civil suit for the crash was settled in July, with Rice set to pay $1 million (plus lawyers' fees) to the two plaintiffs; the lawsuit with his ex-girlfriend is still awaiting trial.

Rice filed for Chapter 7 bankruptcy, which will result in the liquidation and sale of assets to help repay debts, rather than Chapter 13, which would create a payment plan using his regular income.

In the filing, Rice reportedly claimed $677,054 in personal assets, which includes $421,825 in "deferred compensation." Other assets reportedly listed include a Mercedes-Benz worth $53,000, an apartment lease worth $3,500, and $5,000 in NFL jerseys and hats. Rice also placed his Super Bowl LVIII ring, which he valued at $160,000, as collateral, per ESPN .

Rice is in the final year of a four-year rookie deal worth $6,085,657 in total compensation, per Spotrac .

As part of the fallout from the Dallas crash, Rice was sentenced to five years' probation and 30 days in jail in July. He served a six-game suspension from the NFL to start the 2025 season.

Rice served his jail sentence over the summer, calling it "a learning experience and "a reality check" after he returned to Chiefs training camp in August. He has played in five games this season, missing two games last month after suffering a hamstring injury .
